questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place that had both cultural and academic opportunities. It was important to expand my english and therefore it should also be a country where they were speaking english etc. I think this was a great place to go, because it had a good university but besides that all the opportunities outside of the university, and not school-wise, were big and great too. And in the end I really wanted to go somewhere far away that could expand my horizon and let me explore new cultures, nature, activities, people etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really receive any assistance but quickly sought it out myself and then got help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started living on campus but later moved out because a friend had an available room in an apartment - therefore pretty easy to find, however it is not in general.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to live off campus you should start looking early and be patient!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not satisfied with living on campus

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You got a login (a profile) to a special web page where you among others could find possible courses and register for/switch them etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: On the web page different options of help was possible and you could also contact someone if necessary

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was pretty successful - in the beginning a lot of the courses were already full but during the first weeks it was possible for students to shop around, and that gave room for registering and trying out the classes I found interesting. In the end I had a good idea of most of them and could pick from that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Give yourself the opportunity to shop around and get an idea about the different classes, because you cannot be sure about them before you join them/try them out. And be quick to register if you have your eyes on something special - check the courses regarding how full they are.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varied - some of them were challenging while others were more easygoing and not that challenging. However studying in another language and in thise case another law system, and just country in general, is already a more challenging factor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In all classes there were more than one teacher. It was a whole other way of teaching and building up a class than back at UCPH, but of course the different law system also played a role there.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Asian Legal Systems 
Topics in Comparative Law 
Conflicts of Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't have any recommendations - I think it depends on your own preferences and interests etc.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A higher rent when moving away from campus.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some of the groceries and food were more expensive. The rent in general.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different kinds of sports, clubs and sororities/fraternities. And also a museum close by etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Perhaps joining a club because it opens up for you socially and is a fun way to try something new and staying stimulated while being away.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: So much!! It is a wonderful place with a lot of great trips/activities close by or within reach - go hiking, camping, explore the city, take a trip etc. Look up all the stuff you can do and go.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All of it - I like expanding my horizon.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be openminded and prepared for it to be different than back home
2) You can always get help but are also somewhat on your own so take up the challenge 
3) Be aware of the housing situation

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: People are sweet and helpful so don't be afraid to ask for help - and be open socially in general.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of it - it was a fantastic experience!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being in another country so far away and studying in another language and in my case law system, however it was an experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I will absolutely recommend going on exchange - and UBC (and BC/Canada) is a great place also, so I can recommend!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
